name: Network Implant / Backdoor
description: The LAN Turtle is a covert network implant that provides remote access to the target network by establishing an outbound tunnel. Placed inline between a computer and network port — disguised as a USB Ethernet adapter — it creates a persistent network foothold that survives reboots. It includes modules for network scanning, credential capture, and reverse shell establishment, and its outbound-only connection model avoids many perimeter firewall restrictions.

blue.det: New unknown device on DHCP logs; NAC policy violation alert; unusual outbound connection from unknown MAC; C2 traffic patterns.
blue.cm: Network Access Control (NAC); 802.1X port authentication; DHCP monitoring for unknown MACs; network segmentation; regular physical network port audits.
